'''Carmela González Troncoso''' (born 1982 in [[Vigo]]) is a Spanish [[Telecommunications engineering|telecommunication engineer]] and [[research]]er specialized in [[Privacy|privacy issues]], and an [[LGBT|LGBT+]] activist. She is currently a scientific director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carmela Troncoso becomes a new scientific director at the MPI for Security and Privacy |url=https://www.mpi-sp.org/73502/news_publication_23967271_transferred |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=www.mpi-sp.org |language=en}}</ref> on leave from [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) in [[Switzerland]]. She is the head of the SPRING lab (Security and Privacy Engineering Laboratory).<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|date=10 June 2017|title=Dr Carmela Troncoso named Tenure Track Assistant Professor|work=EPFL News|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/dr-carmela-troncoso-named-tenure-track-assistant-2/|access-date=11 June 2020}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=The lab|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/spring/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-US}}</ref> Troncoso gained recognition for her leadership of the European team developing the [[DP-3T]] protocol that aims at the creation of an application to facilitate the tracing of [[COVID-19]] infected persons without compromising on the privacy of citizens.<ref>{{Cite news|title=First pilot for the Google and Apple-based decentralised tracing app|work=Swiss Science Today|url=https://www.sciena.ch/research/first-pilot-for-the-google-and-applebased-decentralised-tracing-app.html|access-date=11 June 2020|archive-date=11 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611140633/https://www.sciena.ch/research/first-pilot-for-the-google-and-applebased-decentralised-tracing-app.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|date=2020-05-07|title=European coalition takes shape on coronavirus contact tracing|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-europe-tech-idUSKBN22J1N8|access-date=2020-08-13}}</ref><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|last=Farr|first=Christina|date=2020-04-28|title=How a handful of Apple and Google employees came together to help health officials trace coronavirus|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/28/apple-iphone-contact-tracing-how-it-came-together.html|access-date=2020-08-21|website=CNBC|language=en}}</ref> Currently she is also member of the Swiss National COVID-19 Science Task Force in the expert group on Digital Epidemiology.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=ncs-tf.ch: Topics & Expert groups|url=https://ncs-tf.ch/en/topics-expert-groups#digital_epidemiology|access-date=2020-08-21|website=ncs-tf.ch}}</ref> In 2020, she was listed among [[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune magazine's]] [[40 Under 40]].<ref name=":7" />

== Career ==
Troncoso studied [[engineering]] at [[University of Vigo]] and in 2006 graduated in [[Telecommunications engineering|telecommunication engineering]]. She went to [[KU Leuven]] to work on her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] on "Design and analysis methods for privacy technologies" under the supervision of [[Bart Preneel]] and Claudia Díaz.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Troncos|first=Carmela|title=Design and analysis methods for privacy technologies|url=http://carmelatroncoso.com/papers/CTroncoso-PhD2011.pdf|access-date=2020-08-21}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Carmela Troncoso's HomePage|url=http://carmelatroncoso.com/|access-date=2020-08-12|website=carmelatroncoso.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Former members {{!}} COSIC|url=https://www.esat.kuleuven.be/cosic/former-members/|access-date=2020-08-12|language=nl}}</ref> She continued at KU Leuven as a post-doc before joining [[Gradiant (foundation)|Gradiant]], the Galician Research and Development Center in Advanced Telecommunications, as a Security and Privacy Technical Lead. In October 2015 Troncoso joined the [[IMDEA Software Institute]] (Spain) as faculty member.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Carmela Troncoso - IMDEA Software Institute|url=https://software.imdea.org/people/carmela.troncoso/index.html|access-date=2020-08-12|website=software.imdea.org}}</ref> Since November 2017 she has been a tenure track assistant professor at the SPRING lab (Security and Privacy Engineering Laboratory)<ref name=":4" /> at the School of Computer and Communication Sciences<ref>{{Cite web|title=School of Computer and Communication Sciences|url=https://www.epfl.ch/schools/ic/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) in [[Switzerland]].<ref name=":2" />

== Research ==
Troncoso's research focuses on technologies enabling the development of socially responsible systems such as machine learning, privacy evaluation and privacy-preserving systems:<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":0" />

* Machine learning: Troncoso studies the impact of machine learning algorithms on daily activities of contemporary society, both the improvements as well as the disadvantages. Employing machine learning she builds tools helping to enhance system designs and find ethical designs defending against machine learning-based attacks on privacy.
* Privacy evaluation: Her lab performs research that helps user to authorize to better understand how much information they reveal, and to enable software developers to achieve their goals without endangering the privacy of users.
* Engineering privacy-preserving systems: Troncoso also works on developing frameworks assisting engineers to build privacy-preserving systems and methodologies that allow them to assess in a systematic way about the design and the evaluation of privacy-preserving technologies.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":0" />

Based on her research, and together with [[International Consortium of Investigative Journalists]] (ICIJ) Troncoso developed the opensource collaborative data analysis tool Datashare.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Datashare - ICIJ|url=https://datashare.icij.org/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=datashare.icij.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-08-17|title='Trust and technology' at heart of latest collaborative journalism tool|url=http://www.icij.org/inside-icij/2020/08/trust-and-technology-at-heart-of-latest-collaborative-journalism-tool/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=ICIJ|language=en-US}}</ref> Datashare was used in the analysis of the Luanda Leaks.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Luanda Leaks {{!}} Africa's richest woman exploited family ties, shell companies and inside deals|language=en-US|work=ICIJ|url=https://www.icij.org/investigations/luanda-leaks/|access-date=2020-08-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=How we mined more than 715,000 Luanda Leaks records|url=https://www.icij.org/investigations/luanda-leaks/how-we-mined-more-than-715000-luanda-leaks-records/|access-date=2020-08-21|website=ICIJ|date=3 February 2020|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Covid-19 pandemic ==
In 2020, during the crisis of the Covid-19 pandemic, she leads a team of more than 30 people from eleven European institutions working to develop the [[DP-3T]] protocol under the umbrella of the [[Pan-European Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing]] (PEPP-PT) to create a computer application that tracks contacts and at the same time respects privacy with the aim of letting citizens know if they have been close to someone who days later tests positive for the virus.<ref>{{Cite web|title=HOME {{!}} PEPP-PT|url=https://www.pepp-pt.org/|access-date=2020-08-12|website=Pepp Pt|language=de|archive-date=2020-04-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200409221119/https://www.pepp-pt.org/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> She is first author of white paper on the application of the [[Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing|DP-3T]] protocol.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web == Distinctions ==
In September 2020, Troncoso joined the ranks of "40 influential people" ([[40 Under 40]]) in the category technology nominated by the  [[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] magazine.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|title=Carmela Troncoso {{!}} 2020 40 under 40 in Tech|url=https://fortune.com/40-under-40/2020/carmela-troncoso/|access-date=2020-09-16|website=Fortune|language=en}}</ref>

Since 2020 Troncoso has been a member of the Swiss National COVID-19 Science Task Force, the scientific corona advisory board of the [[Federal Council (Switzerland)|Swiss Federal Council]] and the [[Cantons of Switzerland|cantons]]. She is a member of the expert group on Digital Epidemiology.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=ncs-tf.ch: Organisation|url=https://ncs-tf.ch/de/organisation|access-date=2020-09-14|website=ncs-tf.ch}}</ref>

She is an awardee of the ERCIM WG STM Best Ph.D. Thesis Award (2011),<ref>{{Cite web|title=ERCIM Working group|url=https://www.iit.cnr.it/STM-WG/contentpage06.html|access-date=2020-08-12|website=www.iit.cnr.it}}</ref> the CNIL-INRIA Privacy Protection Award 2017 (Paper: Engineering privacy by design reloaded)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Inria and the CNIL award the 2017 privacy protection prize to a European research team {{!}} CNIL|url=https://www.cnil.fr/en/inria-and-cnil-award-2017-privacy-protection-prize-european-research-team|access-date=2020-08-12|website=www.cnil.fr}}</ref> and the Google Security and Privacy Research Award (2019).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Luterbacher|first=Celia|date=February 22, 2019 |title=Carmela Troncoso wins Google Security and Privacy Research Award|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/carmela-troncoso-wins-google-security-and-privac-7/|language=en |access-date=April 19, 2021}}</ref>
